To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Frenkel pairs in KBr and KCI, created by X-ray irradiation at low temperatures, were identified by combined length change and X-ray diffraction measurements.
Frenkel defects are created in alkali halide crystals by low-temperature irradiation.
the volume change of different Frenkel defects in the alkali-halides KBr andKCl was measured.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: - The influence of the lattice parameter on the energy of defects - The volume change of Frenkel defects and the influence of the defect type on the lattice distortion - The influence of Frenkel pairs on the energy of the defects.
the determination of the volume change and lattice distortion caused by different types of Frenkel pairs in KBr and KCI.
the following problems: (1) The influence of lattice distortions due to Frenkel pairs and their volume change on the lattice parameter of alkali halides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Frenkel disorder in alkali halides can be considered as an ideal model for the study of defect structure and properties.
Frenkel disorder is created by low energy radiation, and that the volume changes of the different defects are different.

the lattice parameter and length measurements are very suitable to determine the type of disorder in alkali halides and that the lattice parameter change is a good measure of the volume change of the lattice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Frenkel disorder in KBr is caused by the creation of two Frenkel pairs.
the volume change due to a defect depends on the type of defect, the lattice constant of the host crystal, and the number of the nearest neighbors of the defect.

the Frenkel disorder in alkali halides is not a homogeneous distribution of point defects but consists of different pairs of Frenkel defects, which are created by the different energy of the primary radiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Frenkel pairs in KBr and KI can be distinguished by their volume change.
the Frenkel pair ofα- and I-center causes a volume increase of 3.2 atomic unit cells and the Frenkel pairs of F- andH-center a volume increase of only 1.2 atomic unit cell.
the Frenkel defects created in KBr by X-ray radiation are of two different types, one consisting ofα- center andI-center and the other ofF-center andH-center.
